root_idea.summary: The root centers on approaching or seeking something, especially through nocturnal ranging or pursuit, alongside a distinct branch of lightness, scantness, or reduced quantity.
root_idea.development: The simple verb extends from night patrol and searching to agent nouns and derived seeking constructions. The reduplicated form describes the night at either boundary—approaching and darkening or departing—while the departure sense is also analyzed as an inversion related to سَعْسَعَ. The lightness branch appears in scant feeding and reluctant or limited milk yield.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Displayed under the normalized Form I perfect citation form عَسْعَسَ.

senses.definition: For the night to approach or come on, with darkness arriving.
senses.usage_conditions: Used of the night at its beginning; the lexical tradition also records the related sense of the night being dark, potentially throughout the night.

senses.definition: For the night or its darkness to depart or recede.
senses.usage_conditions: Used of the night at its end. The form is reported with opposite readings in the Quranic expression, and this reading is the one reflected by the supplied contextual gloss.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To go about by night in search or pursuit; to patrol, investigate suspicious persons, seek prey or sustenance, or range to and fro.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of a person, wolf, or other beast of prey; the nocturnal searching sense may include smelling out prey.

other_classical_meanings.definition: For tidings to be slow or tardy.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A predicative use concerning the delay of news or tidings.

other_classical_meanings.definition: For a she-camel to yield little milk or to yield it unwillingly, sometimes with repeated grumbling during milking.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A camel-specific use covering scant or reluctant milk production.

other_classical_meanings.definition: For a she-camel to pasture alone.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A camel-specific use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To be parsimonious with someone in one's wealth.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Occurs with عَلَى in the cited construction.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To seek or track someone or something; by night, to search for prey or sustenance, trace footsteps, or pursue vice.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The transitive construction may take a person, thing, traces, or an abstract object.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To feed a people or party with a small or scant quantity of food.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A causative feeding construction.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To travel through a country and learn its conditions or news.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Form VIII derived seeking construction.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To seek or obtain a she-camel's milk, including by entering among camels and stroking their udders to induce milk yield.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Form VIII construction used with camels or a she-camel's milk.

other_classical_meanings.definition: In the expression عَسِّكَ وَبِسِّكَ, from wherever one can obtain it; from any or every quarter.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An idiomatic expression meaning roughly “from where it is and where it is not” or “whence you will.”

other_classical_meanings.definition: A large drinking cup or bowl, larger than an ordinary قَدَح and sufficient for two or more people to drink from.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Plural forms include عِسَاسٌ, عِسَسَةٌ, and أَعْسَاسٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Something apparent, manifest, or conspicuous.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An assumed figurative use in the expression عَلَى ظَهْرِ العُسِّ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The penis.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An anatomical noun.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Slowness or tardiness.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A verbal-noun or abstract nominal use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Covetous merchants or traders.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A plural or collective designation for traders characterized by avidity.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Large vessels or containers.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A nominal plural use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A trace, footprint, vestige, or similar indication left behind.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A nominal use for evidence of passage or remaining indication.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The thinness or attenuation of darkness.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Associated with the two edges of the night.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A seeker or pursuer of prey, especially by night; by extension, a wolf or other beast of prey, or a dog that pursues persistently and will not eat.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An agent noun applied to animals characterized by repeated searching or pursuit.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A she-camel that yields little or reluctant milk, delays before yielding it, circles away when approached for milking, grumbles, kicks, or spills the milk.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A camel-specific adjective with several reported descriptions of difficult or conditional milking.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A she-camel that pastures alone.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A camel-specific use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A she-camel that searches for bones and eats the flesh remaining on them.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A camel-specific feeding description.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A woman who does not mind men approaching her, or who ventures into conduct that occasions suspicion or evil opinion.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A gender-specific personal description explicitly reported for this adjective.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A man in whom there is little or no goodness, or who does little good.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A personal description of deficient goodness or benefit.

other_classical_meanings.definition: One who is slow or tardy.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An adjectival personal description.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A mirage.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A nominal use distinct from the reduplicated night verb.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Hedgehogs.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A plural designation explained by their frequent going to and fro by night.

other_classical_meanings.definition: One who patrols or goes the rounds by night, especially to guard people and investigate suspicious persons; also any seeker of a thing.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used for a nocturnal patrolman or, more broadly, a seeker.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A place where something is sought or may be sought.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A place noun synonymous with مَطْلَبٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: For a wolf to approach something while sniffing it.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Form II reduplicated construction describing an animal's approach in search of something.

other_classical_meanings.definition: For clouds to approach the earth at night.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional nocturnal construction, especially when darkness and lightning are present.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A place or locality called عَسْعَسٌ.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An isolated nominal usage reported as outside the principal semantic branches.

cautions: عَسْعَسَ in 81:17 is a reported contronym: the supplied lexical evidence preserves both the approach or darkening of night and its departure. The contextual Quran gloss supports the departure reading but does not by itself establish the lexical senses. This entry does not treat Lane's historical citation notation as an additional modern verse location.
